Active partnership program — technology ecosystem play
weaknesses: Pure tech play — no advisory or implementation layer
No DPDP compliance expertise or India regulatory mapping

battlecards.win_strategy: Position TC as the advisory + implementation partner SpotDraft customers need. Don't compete on CLM tech — compete on the human advisory layer. Pursue certified partner status to turn SpotDraft's customer base into TC's pipeline.

battlecards.name: Legistify
strengths: India-focused litigation management SaaS — growing enterprise adoption
Strong position in Indian corporate legal teams
Simple, focused product — litigation tracking and management
weaknesses: Narrow focus — litigation only; no contract, compliance, or advisory offering
Cannot serve the full legal ops stack enterprises need
No cross-border capabilities or international compliance
No GCC-specific offering despite India's GCC boom
battlecards.win_strategy: Out-position by offering full-stack legal ops including litigation oversight as one component. TC handles everything Legistify can't — contracts, compliance, DPDP, fractional GC, employment law. Position as 'Legistify + everything else.'

battlecards.name: Harvey AI

Deep AI/LLM capabilities — contract analysis, research, drafting

Prefer pure-tech self-serve over advisory model

cards.title: ALSP Market Hits $28.5B — 18% CAGR
cards.body: The Alternative Legal Service Provider market reached $28.5 billion with an 18% compound annual growth rate. CLD adoption stands at 57% globally, with the UK leading at 65%. India's GCC boom (183 new centres in H1 2026) is creating the fastest-growing addressable market for legal ops outsourcing.

cards.title: ALSP Consolidation Wave — M&A Reshaping Landscape
cards.body: Repario-UnitedLex merger + Bloomberg Law's consolidation analysis signal structural shift in ALSP market. PE firms driving roll-ups. Combined entities offer broader services but face integration complexity — advisory demand rising. LawVu-ClauseBase expands platform plays.

cards.title: 61% of US In-House Teams Deploying GenAI — But Gap Remains
cards.body: 61% of US in-house teams have deployed or are piloting GenAI. But mid-market adoption lags — only 34% of sub-1000 employee companies have started. AT&T's LegalEdge sets the enterprise benchmark. TC opportunity: Bridge the AI-legal gap for mid-market companies and Indian GCCs.

cards.title: UK 96% AI Integration — Highest Global Adoption
cards.body: UK leads globally with 96% of firms having integrated AI; 34% investing £100K+. ALSP adoption at 65% — also highest globally. But Digital Security & AI Bill creates new compliance requirements. TC opportunity: UK GCCs in India face dual compliance burden.

cards.title: India GCC Boom Creates Legal Ops Demand Surge
cards.body: 183 GCCs in H1 2026, 5.1 lakh jobs, $105B market by 2030 (NASSCOM-Zinnov). 66% of new GCC roles are AI/data. But legal ops maturity lags — most GCCs under 300 headcount don't have a full-time GC. TC's FGC offering addresses this exact gap.

cards.title: DPDP Consent Manager — 33-Day Revenue Window
cards.body: 33 days to consent manager deadline. Every data fiduciary processing personal data needs a registered consent manager or faces INR 50 Cr penalty. Estimated 10,000+ enterprises need compliance assessment. TC's CRaaS + FGC offering is the exact solution.

cards.title: Post-Funding Legal Ops — 28 Startups This Week
cards.body: 28 Indian startups raised $123M this week. Each needs legal ops within 48 hours — entity structuring, ESOP, IP assignment, employment agreements, DPDP compliance. TC's ECP offering handles all of this. Conversion target: 5% of funded startups = 1.4 new clients/week.

cld_summary: The CLD landscape presents a three-market opportunity for TC. India's GCC boom (183 centres in H1, $105B market by 2030) creates the largest addressable pipeline — most GCCs under 300 headcount need TC's FGC offering. The 33-day DPDP consent manager deadline is the highest-urgency conversion lever. In the US, legal tech consolidation (Repario-UnitedLex, Harvey at $15.5B) opens partnership channels — TC as the India advisory partner for global platforms. In the UK, dual compliance burden (Digital Security & AI Bill + DPDP for India operations) creates advisory demand from UK GCCs. Bottom line: India is the volume play, US is the partnership play, UK is the premium advisory play.

cards.title: SpotDraft: Platform Play with Network Effects
cards.body: Model: SaaS CLM platform with self-serve + enterprise tiers. Building network effects through contract repository. Active partnership program. Weakness: Pure tech play — no advisory layer, no India-specific compliance expertise. TC angle: Position as the advisory + implementation partner that SpotDraft customers need.

cards.title: Legistify: India-Focused Litigation SaaS
cards.body: Model: Litigation tracking + management platform targeting Indian enterprises. Weakness: Narrow focus on litigation only; no contract, compliance, or advisory offering. TC angle: Out-position by offering full-stack legal ops including litigation oversight as one component.

cards.title: Harvey AI: GenAI Leader — Partner, Not Compete
cards.body: Model: GenAI platform for law firms and enterprises. $15.5B valuation. 80+ Am Law firms. AT&T LegalEdge validates enterprise model. Key insight: Harvey serves a different segment (AI tooling vs advisory). TC play: Be the India advisory partner for enterprises adopting Harvey-style AI legal tools.

cards.title: Vakilsearch & LawRato: SME Marketplace Models
cards.body: Model: High-volume, low-ACV marketplace connecting lawyers with SMEs and individuals. Weakness: Commoditised services, no enterprise capability. TC angle: Completely different segment — TC targets enterprise/GCCs. No direct conflict, but guard against down-market drift.

cards.title: Partnership Model: Ecosystem vs. Solo Play
cards.body: SpotDraft and Harvey AI have built tech that TC's clients need. Rather than competing, TC should embed as the advisory layer in their ecosystems. Play: Certified implementation partner for SpotDraft India, referral arrangements with compliance-tech platforms. Comp AI ($34M) needs India market expertise — ideal partnership target.

cards.title: Operations: Tech-Enabled vs Pure Tech
cards.body: Pure tech competitors (SpotDraft, Volody, Kira) solve one layer of the legal ops stack. TC's advantage: human expertise + tech enablement. GCCs need someone to run the India legal function, not just a dashboard. Key metric: TC resolves 90%+ of matters without external counsel referral — competitors can't match this.

cards.title: DPDP Specialisation — Temporal Moat
cards.body: No pure-tech competitor can deliver DPDP compliance advisory at the depth TC can. The 33-day consent manager deadline is a temporal moat — clients need human expertise NOW, not in 6 months. After Nov 13: enforcement actions create ongoing advisory demand. This is TC's strongest competitive lever.

competitors_summary: TC's competitive landscape has three tiers. HIGH threat (SpotDraft, Legistify): Direct India-market competitors — counter with full-stack advisory positioning and pursue partnership instead of head-to-head competition. MEDIUM threat (Harvey AI, Volody, Kira, Practical Law): Adjacent segment players — explore partnership channels (TC as India advisory layer). LOW threat (Vakilsearch, LawRato, Clio, Tessaract): Different segments entirely — no action needed. The AT&T-OpenAI LegalEdge deal (Oct 8) is a game-changer: it validates enterprise AI-legal adoption and creates a wave TC can ride as the advisory + implementation partner. TC's temporal moat is the 33-day DPDP consent manager deadline — no pure-tech player can match TC's compliance advisory depth in this window.

offerings_summary: The Growth Playbook integrates three channels into a unified engine: Outbound (trigger-based outreach on funding, DPDP deadlines, GCC launches, leadership changes, regulatory shifts, and M&A), Inbound (DPDP compliance hub, GCC thought leadership, Knowledge Engine as lead magnet, SEO dominance, and engagement scoring), and Partnerships (tech platform ecosystem with SpotDraft/Comp AI, Big 4 referral network, UK ALSP delivery, and industry association collaboration). The 33-day DPDP deadline is the highest-urgency lever across all three channels. AT&T's LegalEdge launch (Oct 8) creates a new content angle: AI legal compliance advisory. 90-day targets: 50 qualified pipeline leads, 10 DPDP assessments, 5 GCC fractional GC contracts, 2 tech partnerships signed, and 1 UK ALSP MOU.
